s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the manubrium with a history of previous thyroid surgery
salient_findings: Lytic lesion replacing the manubrium on CT imaging
Follicular thyroid cells on fine-needle aspiration
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Previous resection of a large left substernal thyroid lobe 12 years ago
Swelling of the manubrium is slightly tender
Swelling increased in size over the month prior to presentation
CT imaging shows a lytic lesion replacing the manubrium
Lytic lesion is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells
Pathological examination shows thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae

s4.champion: Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma with Osseous Involvement

raw.champion: Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma with Osseous Involvement
raw.rationale: The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae, as shown by pathological examination, and the history of previous substernal thyroid lobe resection suggest local invasion of thyroid cancer into the bone, which is most consistent with follicular thyroid carcinoma with osseous involvement.

rejected.label: Hürthle Cell Carcinoma with Local Invasion
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence of Hürthle cell features in the provided information.

rejected.label: Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma with Bony Metastasis
rejected.why: The fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells, not papillary thyroid cells, which are characteristic of papillary thyroid carcinoma.

rejected.label: Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma with Distant Metastasis
rejected.why: There is no indication of medullary thyroid carcinoma, such as the presence of amyloid deposits or elevated calcitonin levels, in the provided information.

rejected.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: While follicular thyroid carcinoma is a possible diagnosis, the specific involvement of the bone (osseous involvement) is better captured by 'Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma with Osseous Involvement'.
